page.title: Moroccan Nationality Eligibility Test | Ezra Maroc
page.description: Find out in two minutes whether your family allows you to obtain Moroccan nationality by descent. Free test, no commitment.
page.intro: About ten questions, around two minutes: a first indicative assessment of your situation.
page.noscript: This test requires JavaScript. You can also
page.noscriptLink: describe your situation to us directly
page.privacy: Your answers stay in your browser: nothing is stored or sent unless you choose to send it to us.

ui.send: Send my answers to an expert
ui.sendNote: Your answers will be attached to the contact form: you can add your personal message before sending.
ui.disclaimer: This result is an indicative assessment based solely on your answers. It does not constitute legal advice and does not replace an analysis of your file. The decision rests with the competent Moroccan authorities.

questions.label: Moroccan ancestors
questions.text: Who in your family is or was a Moroccan national?

options.text: A grandparent on my father's side
A grandparent on my mother's side
No one, as far as I know

questions.label: Ancestor considered
questions.text: For the next questions, which ancestor do you choose? Pick the one for whom you have the most documents.

options.text: Born in Morocco, has always lived there
Born in Morocco, left between 1956 and 1970

questions.label: Moroccan documents available
questions.text: Which Moroccan documents of this person do you have, or can you obtain?

options.text: Moroccan family record book (livret d'état civil)
Old Moroccan passport or identity card

questions.label: Precedent in the family
questions.text: Has a member of your family already obtained Moroccan papers (nationality certificate, passport, identity card) through this same person?

questions.label: Records proving the links
questions.text: Do you have the records proving each family link between this person and you (births, marriages)?

questions.label: Spelling of names
questions.text: Are first names and surnames spelled the same way on all documents?

questions.label: Parents married
questions.text: Were your parents married when you were born?

questions.label: Country of residence
questions.text: Which country do you live in?

options.text: Obtain a Moroccan passport or identity card
Pass the nationality on to my children
A project in Morocco (settling, investing, retiring)

favorable.label: Favorable situation
favorable.text: Your link with a Moroccan ancestor appears to be provable with documents: this is the most favorable situation for Moroccan nationality to be passed on by descent (Article 6 of the Moroccan Nationality Code). It remains to be checked that your documents are complete and compliant.
favorable.next: A free first discussion to review your documents and the steps to take.

etudier.label: Situation to be assessed
etudier.text: Moroccan nationality is passed on by descent, including over several generations, but each link between your Moroccan ancestor and you will have to be proven by official records. Your file deserves a careful analysis of the documents available and of those missing.
etudier.next: A free first discussion to identify the documents to gather and the strategy best suited to your family.

recherche.label: Document search needed
recherche.text: Without any Moroccan documents for now, the first step is to find your family's records. In many cases, records can be found in the Moroccan civil registers: this is the purpose of our research service.
recherche.next: A free first discussion to gather what you know about your family and see where to start the search.

hors.label: No Moroccan descent identified
hors.text: Based on your answers, no link of descent to a Moroccan national appears. Moroccan nationality can sometimes be acquired in other ways, for example through marriage, under certain conditions.
hors.next: Tell us about your situation: we will let you know whether a procedure is possible.

tips.il: Israeli records (birth, marriage) will need a paper apostille: a printout of an e-Apostille is not accepted in Morocco.
tips.default: Depending on your country, some records will need to be apostilled or translated: we will tell you exactly which ones.
